conceptual_explanation: Level 5 Inversion Mastery focuses on formal academic and legal phrases like 'Under no circumstances' and 'Little did I know'. We also introduce 'Conditional Inversion', where we remove 'if' and swap the verb and subject (e.g., 'Had I known' instead of 'If I had known').

rule_cards.name: The 'Little' Trap
rule_cards.correct: Little did he know that a surprise was waiting for him.

rule_cards.name: Absolute Prohibitions
rule_cards.formula: Under no circumstances / At no time + Aux + Subject + Verb
rule_cards.correct: Under no circumstances should you leave the building.
rule_cards.incorrect: Under no circumstances you should leave...

rule_cards.name: Conditional Inversion (Type 2 & 3)
rule_cards.correct: Had I realized the cost, I wouldn't have bought it.

rule_cards.name: Rarely & Scarcely
rule_cards.correct: Rarely have we seen such dedication in a student.

head_noun_tasks.explanation: 'Little' at the start triggers the auxiliary 'did' before the subject 'the detective'.
This formal negative phrase requires the verb 'are' before 'students'.
'Had' at the start replaces 'If the company had' and requires inversion.
'At no time' triggers the past tense inversion 'did she'.

drill_tasks.question: Little ________ that the company was about to go bankrupt.
Under no circumstances ________ the emergency exit unless there is a fire.
________ I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
Rarely ________ such a talented musician at such a young age.
At no time ________ the truth during the entire trial.

boss_fight.paragraph: Little I suspected that the plan was a trick. Under no circumstances you are allowed to share this secret. Had I known the truth, I would never help him.

errors.explanation: In Type 3 conditionals (Had I known), the main clause must use 'would have + past participle'.

success_feedback: Outstanding! You're using some of the most sophisticated formal structures in English. Your range is impressive.
suggested_next_steps: Master 'No sooner... than' and 'In no way' triggers.
Study how 'So' and 'Neither' can trigger inversion in short responses.
